goal_alignment.note: The newest proposal, prop_e33e6001 ('Footprint-robust temporal atlas of NYC Citi Bike use, 2023-2024'), still delivers Q1-Q3 (monthly seasonality with peak/trough, day-of-week x hour heatmaps with weekday/weekend and commute-peak indices, member vs casual) for both 2023 and 2024. It adds a full-system vs balanced-station-cohort sensitivity layer. It is descriptive and non-causal, with a stop-if-no-data rule and a 3-5 finding report, all as the objective requires. It drops the optional Q4 (weather) explicitly, which the brief permits. The added angle is modest but justified: it reacts to the screening feedback that earlier proposals were incremental.

completeness.note: Ideation round_0 has three proposal files (prop_b1725fb8, prop_4423de20, prop_e33e6001) and meeting_state.finished.json. Each has hypothesis, methods, expected outcomes, alternatives, falsification checks, unresolved disagreements and a decision rationale. All three seats presented and a selection was recorded. Gaps: 'meeting_notes' is empty and every decision has mode 'independent', so no real cross-seat discussion took place; all three decisions pick the proposal from the seat that wrote it, or another one, without debate. 'score' is null and 'selected' is false on all proposals, which is expected before screening. artifacts.json is still at its initial empty state (no observations, no claims), which is fine at this stage.

correctness.note: No numerical results exist yet, so nothing is fabricated. Claims are largely flagged as unverified ('my claim, unverified'). Points to watch in screening: (1) phases/screening/round_0/score.json scores the OLDER weather-elasticity proposal (prop_4423de20, composite 5.75, which the topic text says was rejected). It does not score prop_e33e6001, so the current proposal has not been screened yet. Screening must not reuse that stale score. (2) The headline hypothesis is partly mechanical: a cohort defined as stations observed in all 24 months excludes every 2024 entrant by construction, so 'cohort growth < systemwide growth' is nearly guaranteed. The informative quantity is the size of the gap, and the 5-percentage-point refutation threshold is self-described as arbitrary. (3) The cohort definition (>=1 trip every month in both years) biases towards busy, year-round stations and drops seasonal or winter-closed stations, which could distort the seasonal peak/trough in the cohort. The proposal acknowledges survivorship but offers only a 10-month sensitivity variant. (4) External facts (194 new stations in FY2024, 2,000th station in Sept 2023, 2024 pricing change) come from web snippets, some with utm_source=openai tags, and were not verified by the auditor.

traceability.note: Each proposal's rationale, citations and contributions are stored in its JSON, and the selection reasons are in meeting_state.finished.json and the 'decision' field. Citations are given as URLs or DOIs, though some are search-redirect links (vertexaisearch grounding URLs in prop_4423de20 / b1725fb8 contributions) that are not stable. The container check (read-only docker exec) shows /app is empty (no data files) and curl is not installed. The proposal and screening note correctly say that data and packages are absent and must be downloaded, and that one guessed 2023 filename returned 404. Data availability for both years is therefore still unconfirmed, not established.

summary: Ideation produced three successive proposals after screening rejected the earlier ones as incremental; the latest, prop_e33e6001 (footprint-robust temporal atlas, full system vs a balanced station cohort), covers all required descriptive questions (Q1-Q3), uses a clear cleaning waterfall with 24h/12h sensitivity, keeps results non-causal, has explicit refutation criteria and a stop-if-no-data rule, and is the most feasible of the options (no weather merge, month-by-month aggregation). It is sound enough to hand to screening. Caveats: the only score.json present belongs to a previous proposal, the headline cohort-attenuation hypothesis is partly true by construction, the novelty claim rests on a brief literature search, no discussion occurred in the 'independent' meeting mode, and data availability in the container (2023 file naming, packages) is unverified.
recommendations: Screening must score prop_e33e6001 afresh. phases/screening/round_0/score.json describes prop_4423de20 (weather elasticity, composite 5.75) and must not be treated as the score of the current proposal.

Before committing to the plan, have the next phases confirm data access: list the S3 index (s3.amazonaws.com/tripdata) and determine the exact 2023 and 2024 archive names (2023 appears to be per-year or differently named; a guessed filename returned 404), pip-install duckdb/polars, and stop and report if files cannot be read. Do not generate or simulate data.

Reframe the cohort hypothesis so it is not a near-tautology: report the size of the growth gap and also the share of the 2024-2023 trip difference attributable to entrant stations, and pre-state what counts as a meaningful attenuation. Treat the 5 pp threshold as a reporting convention, not evidence.

Add a seasonal-closure check for the balanced cohort (stations absent in winter months are dropped, which can flatten or shift the seasonal peak/trough) and make the 10-month/year relaxed cohort a required, not optional, sensitivity run.

Keep the descriptive Q1-Q3 deliverables as the primary report content so the 3-5 findings each have a figure, and treat the footprint analysis as a robustness layer. Q4 (weather) may be skipped, but the report should state that it was skipped and why.

State in the report that rider-type definition (member_casual) and bike-type mix changed over time, and that the e-bike/pricing changes in Jan 2024 cannot be separated from behaviour in these data. Verify the external station-count claims against primary sources before citing them.
